title: Mouse Without Borders Portable 1.2.0-preview.6
summary: Restores missing peer connections after display wake, sleep and network address changes, with continuous bounded retries.
changes: Network address changes and display-on notifications schedule coalesced recovery, even when Windows still reports an available network.
Missing peers are retried continuously with bounded backoff. One healthy connection no longer hides another missing peer.
A real resume refreshes socket ownership once; ordinary display-off, display-on and address-change events preserve healthy connections and input hooks.
Per-peer attempt leases cover DNS, connection and handshake work. Each connection attempt receives a fresh monotonic retry budget.
Message sockets use TCP keepalive to detect silent disconnections; established idle peers have no application receive-idle timeout.
Retains the optional administrator-launch setting introduced in preview 5. The protected-service payload and Windows security/power settings are not modified.
testing: Release x64 build and self-contained single-file publish passed. 74 recovery/connection checks and 231 existing elevation, service, updater, settings, encryption and transfer regressions passed locally.
The three-project repository check and 3 release metadata tests passed. This is focused validation, not full inherited-suite success.
See docs/CONNECTION_RECOVERY.md for exact local automated results and pending physical two-PC acceptance.
Finish active transfers before replacing the EXE. Keep adjacent preferences and recovery files; a same-path update retains administrator-launch choice.
known_limitations: Windows x64 preview. Real display-off, sleep/wake and adapter-change behavior requires physical acceptance on the affected machines.
Windows can suspend desktop apps and networking during Modern Standby; reconnect runs when the application and network are available again.
Recovery does not automatically resume user-paused file-transfer jobs or bypass a mismatched security key.
Existing updater path restrictions and inherited full-suite failures remain documented.
